revisionNote: REVISED same session on the coordinator's scope change: the original version of this package staged only the 100 plain base/prospect cards and held out every rung and every autograph/insert subset. The 2024 Bowman's Best sales cell is mostly Refractor parallels and autographs, and 'no synthetic parallels' forbids INVENTING rungs, not staging the rungs the Beckett checklist itself lists -- those are scraped source rows and belong in the package. This revision stages the FULL workbook as Beckett lists it: 4,538 rows across the Base, Prospects, Autographs and Inserts sheets, per-parallel rows with the print run the sheet states, isAuto=true for every Autographs-sheet subset, insert-/auto- category prefixes kept. Nothing is held out; see heldOut.

gapThisFills: One of the four genuine-gap checklist acquisitions ordered by Drew 2026-09-28. Cell 2024|bowman-chrome carries 24,422 unbacked sales (raw census label: 'mixed: N-number-resolve + checklist ingest (Bowman's Best/CPA insert)'); the orchestrator-confirmed SPECIFIC gap this package targets is that no year of Bowman's Best had ever had a numbered checklist acquired -- only a parallels vocabulary (data/checklist-parallel-names.json, cell baseball|2024|bowmans-best, 28 names) and a Beckett variations guide existed prior to this package. Because the unbacked volume in that cell is mostly Refractor parallels and autographs, this package stages the whole workbook: the 100 base/prospect cards, their full Refractor-family ladder, and every autograph and insert subset with its own ladder. It does NOT by itself resolve every unbacked sale at 2024|bowman-chrome, since that cell is a distinct, already-registered sibling product (bowman-chrome) and some of its volume is CPA-insert rows that belong to bowman-chrome, not to this product.
sourcePageShape: Beckett xlsx workbook, six sheets: Base (95 raw rows), Prospects (55), Autographs (968), Inserts (1046), Teams (skipped: team-sorted duplicate of the others), Master (skipped: superset sheet). Each sheet lists a card-number column, a player column, and one section per named rung with the print run stated in the section heading. Numbering as printed on the cards: Base #1-70 (veterans/rookies), Prospects TP-1..TP-30, Autographs B24-XX (Best of 2024 Autographs), FGRA-XX (2024 MLB All-Star Futures Game Chrome Autograph Relics), IPA-XX, BBA-XX, FPA-XX, BSA-XX, DA-XX, TA-XXX, QA-XXXX, FDA-XX, FTA-XXX; Inserts IP-N, BB-N, FP-N, FG-N, BS-N, SG-N, BA-N. Every prefix is unique to its subset, so no two subsets share an address.
converterNote: Converted with the sanctioned scripts/convertBeckettChecklistXlsx.cjs (--xlsx <path> --year 2024 --set-key bowmans-best --set-name "2024 Bowman's Best" --sport baseball --out 2024-bowmans-best-baseball.raw.csv --source-url <sourceUrl> --source-label beckett-s3-2026-09-28). Converter output: wrote 2024-bowmans-best-baseball.raw.csv; rows=4538 (deduped 0); by kind: {"base":1900,"auto":2145,"insert":493}; sections: 20 (anchors 2, parallels 0, own-cards 18). The committed CSV is the converter's raw output with ONE change: the 60-row spelling harmonisation described under spellingHarmonization. No rows added, none dropped, no other field touched. Print runs and isAuto flags are the converter's own reading of the sheet section headings and of which SHEET a row sat on (Autographs -> isAuto=true), never inferred from player text.

spellingHarmonization.scope: Only the 30 Prospects-sheet TP- cards x these two rungs (30 + 30 = 60 rows). The 70 Base-sheet cards already carry the singular spelling.
spellingHarmonization.why: The workbook spells the SAME rung two ways across its two base-roster sheets: 'Mini-Diamond Refractors /299' and 'Green Mini-Diamond Refractors /99' on the Base sheet, 'Mini-Diamonds Refractors /299' and 'Green Mini-Diamonds Refractors /99' on the Prospects sheet -- identical print run, identical ladder position, one product. computeHobbyIqCardId singularises only the TRAILING word of a parallel ('Refractors' -> refractor, harmless), not an inner word, so 'Mini-Diamonds Refractors' slugs to `mini-diamonds-refractor` and 'Mini-Diamond Refractors' to `mini-diamond-refractor`: two ids, two pools, for one card class -- exactly the split 'one card, one row, one pool' forbids. The Base sheet's spelling is kept because (a) it is the majority spelling in the workbook itself, (b) it is the spelling the existing vocabulary cell baseball|2024|bowmans-best already carries ('Mini-Diamond Refractor', 'Green Mini-Diamond Refractor'), and (c) an in-repo census of data/*.json finds 'Mini-Diamond Refractor(s)' 136 times against 'Mini-Diamonds Refractor' 18. This is a spelling correction of the source's own inconsistency, not a new rung: both rungs exist in the source with these print runs. Flagged in the PR as the one reviewable judgment call in this package.
spellingHarmonization.verifiedBy: bowmansBest2024BaseChecklistMatchesPlannerVerdict.test.ts pins that the harmonised spelling reaches the same id as the singular vocabulary form and that the plural inner-word form would not, and that neither 'Mini-Diamonds' spelling remains in the CSV.

The vocabulary's other 10 names are the auto/insert ladders (Mini-Diamond /25, Lava /50, Red /5, Gold /50, Orange /25, Black /10, Blue /150, Green /99, Purple /250) and agree with the print runs on this file's auto-*/insert-* rows. No print-run disagreement anywhere.

categoryNote: Base and Top Prospects are both category=base (never a separate insert-/auto- category): the TP- prefix already keeps every id distinct from the 1-70 range, so planStagedDirectory measures zero need for subset separation. Every Autographs-sheet subset is auto-<slug> and every Inserts-sheet subset is insert-<slug>, the converter's own category naming, kept verbatim. Because each subset has its own printed prefix, none of these categories ever collides with base or with one another, so no subset is minted onto its own setKey (plan.keys=[]) -- they all ride the plain bowmans-best key with the category preserved on the row for display, exactly as the 2025 Topps Chrome Beckett package's auto/insert rows do.
heldOutNote: Nothing held out in this revision. The planner found no insert prefix that collides and no subset whose key would need registering, so there was no reason to hold any subset; every row the Beckett workbook lists for this product is staged. Rows from the Teams and Master sheets are not 'held out' -- they are the same cards re-sorted, which the converter correctly skips as duplicates.
